newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Suez to protect Tractebel independence -Belgian PM.
newsitem.headline: Suez to protect Tractebel independence -Belgian PM.

text.p: Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene said on Friday that he had received an offer of guarantees from French Compagnie de Suez that the independence of Belgian utility holding company Tractebel SA would not be threathened by a possible merger of Suez with French Lyonnaise des Eaux.

"I think the intention of Suez and (its 63 percent unit Belgian holding company Societe Generale de Belgique SA) SGB is to put these guarantees into force by modifying the statutes of Tractebel at the shareholders meeting which must approve Tractebel's merger with Powerfin," Dehaene told a news conference after the weekly cabinet meeting.
SGB is Suez's biggest asset. Tractebel, which is 65 percent owned by SGB, recently announced plans to merge with its international energy unit Powerfin.

Belgian politicians have expressed fears that a Suez-Lyonnaise merger might threaten the independence of Tractebel which, through its Electrabel and Distrigas units, controls Belgium's gas and electricity sector.
In addition fears have been expressed that Lyonnaise would, after a merger, stop Powerfin from competing for new international energy contracts.
Suez and Lyonnaise ended a week of stock market speculation earlier on Friday with a statement they would discuss merger plans at special board meetings on April 11.
"There is an approach and willingness on both sides to meet the problems raised by the (Belgian) government," Dehaene said.
"I am convinced these (talks) will end with an agreement," he added.
Dehaene said the government had made various proposal as to how Tratctebel's statutes could be modified to guarantee its autonomy. He gave no details.
